newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: GOLF - MITCHELL WINS WITH GREAT FINISH.
newsitem.headline: GOLF - MITCHELL WINS WITH GREAT FINISH.

text.p: A brilliant 130-yard wedge shot to within one foot at the final hole earned Peter Mitchell of Britain a one-stroke victory in the Madeira Island Open on Sunday.

After 22-year-old Swede Fredrik Jacobson had completed an eight-under-par 64 to put the pressure on the 38-year-old Londoner, Mitchell capped a nervous one-under-par 71 with his closing birdie to record his second European Tour victory.
"I felt awful over that last putt because I had missed some close ones earlier," said Mitchell, whose last win was in the 1992 Austrian Open.
The victory earned him 50,000 pounds ($81,500) and pushed him up to 10th spot on the European Ryder Cup list, which could earn him a callup for this September's match.
"I'll have to win another tournament to get in and hopefully I'll make a better job of it the next time I have a chance," he said.
Mitchell, who took a four-shot lead into the final round, missed several opportunities and when he bogeyed the 15th hole, he and Jacobson were level.
One round was lost to bad weather and Mitchell finished with a total of 204, 12 under par.
Jacobson, from Molndal, shot nine birdies with a longest putt of 15 feet and after missing halfway cuts in his last three events he was pleased.
"I was playing without a game plan. Now I've decided on a strategy, thinking how to play every hole, and I'm sticking to it," he said.
Jacobson lost his tour card in 1995 but regained it last year from the Challenger Tour.
Scotsman Andrew Coltart had a chance to tie for second place but missed from six feet at the last. He was third with a 68.
